proof_summary: Take the composite witness \(n=23492890653051=3\cdot37\cdot43\cdot42307\cdot116341\). Multiplicativity of the gcd-sum and the prime-factor formula \(\sum_{k=1}^{p}\gcd(k,p)=2p-1\) give \(\sum_{k=1}^{n}\gcd(k,n)=610815156979325=26n-1\), so the relevant gcd is \(n\) and the quotient equals \(1\), despite \(n\) being composite.
